title: Single Spike Artificial Neural Networks
problem: Standard ANNs require large-scale arithmetic with high energy consumption, while spiking neural networks (SNNs) circumvent this via biologically inspired computation but use fundamentally different algorithms from ANNs, preventing reuse of the mature ANN software stack and optimization techniques. The paper seeks an intermediate approach that achieves the energy efficiency of SNNs while remaining compatible with ANN algorithms and toolchains.
motivation: The growing energy cost of ANN inference drives interest in biologically inspired temporal/spike-based computing, but existing SNNs cannot leverage decades of ANN algorithmic advances and software infrastructure.
method: The design treats each weight as a signal delay and each activation magnitude as a signal's arrival time, replacing standard arithmetic operations. These time-based signals flow through a systolic array—a grid of synchronized processors—using proven data patterns that efficiently reuse the same hardware across both space and time cycles. Between layers, the system sums time-shifted signals using noise-tolerant operations and stores results in hybrid circuits combining digital memory with time-based encoding, while maintaining full compatibility with traditional ANN algorithms.
key_novelty: Encoding ANN weights as delays and activation magnitudes as signal arrival times enables traditional ANN algorithms to run on biologically inspired circuits with 11× better energy than spiking neural networks.
contributions: A temporal computing substrate that maps standard ANN weights to delay elements and activations to signal arrival times, bridging ANN and SNN computation styles
Spatial and temporal reuse strategies enabling classical ANN dataflows (weight-stationary systolic array) within temporal circuits
A noise-tolerant temporal summation operation and hybrid digital/temporal memory for inter-layer activation management
Empirical demonstration using MLPerf Tiny benchmarks showing 11x energy improvement over SNNs and 3.5x over 8-bit digital systolic arrays with 4x latency improvement

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 11x better energy vs SNNs; 3.5x better energy vs 8-bit digital systolic arrays
metrics.accuracy: Inference accuracy evaluated across multiple MLPerf Tiny architectural parameter configurations

limitations: Evaluation limited to MLPerf Tiny benchmark suite; practicality at large model scale and robustness to real circuit noise not fully characterized.
primary_theme: temporal-signal ANN execution for energy-efficient inference
